question.worked_solution:
First, recall that

$$
{lim}_{t\to 0}f(t)=({lim}_{t\to 0}\operatorname{sin}⁡t)i+({lim}_{t\to 0}\operatorname{cos}⁡t)j+({lim}_{t\to 0}(t+2)^{2})k.
$$

Now, we find the limits one-by-one.

- For the first component, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 0}\operatorname{sin}⁡t & =\operatorname{sin}⁡0=0.\end{aligned}
$$

- For the second component, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 0}\operatorname{cos}⁡0=1.\end{aligned}
$$

- For the third component, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 0}\,(t+2)^{2} & =(0+2)^{2}=4.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, ${lim}_{t\to 0}f(t)=j+4\,k.$
